subject: swampTroll
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: swamp troll with tusks, mohawk and bone fetishes.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
Looking closely at the renders, I notice the head seems too small and sunken into the chest with the face obscured, and the tusk placement near the muzzle looks off. The braids hanging down the chest read as thick orange poles rather than hair, which breaks the illusion of texture.

The real issue is that the braid color paint uses the sweep angle variable (0-360 degrees) instead of a proper color value, which pushes it toward orange — I need to swap this for a solid dark red hex color instead. I also want to make the braids thinner and tucked closer to the sides so they don't cover the face and chest so much, and enlarge the tusks so they curve upward past the nose for a more iconic troll look. I'll also thicken the mohawk blades since from the front they currently read as a thin edge-on line.

I'm also considering whether to enlarge the head relative to the body, since the hump geometry currently overlaps the back of the skull. Rather than rescale everything, I think a safer fix is nudging the neck and head position up and slightly forward, while leaving the mohawk and braid attachment points roughly where they are since they're defined relative to the head.

Checking other details: the staff's skull eyes glow nicely even sitting on top rather than in sockets, the right hand placement and arm proportions look fine in three-quarter view, the chest decal and shoulder pauldrons read well, and the loose hip pieces seem to need another look.

The tusks need to be bigger, thicker, and curve outward and upward from a well-seated base—I'm working out the exact curve geometry for where they attach to the jaw relative to the head's local coordinate space.

Actually I realize the bigger issue is that the orange braids are overlapping and hiding the tusks in the front view, so I need to fix the braid placement first: making them darker red, thinner, and repositioning them to start further out near the ear so they don't cover the tusks. Adjusting the braid path coordinates...

I'm switching the braid color to a flat dark red, thickening the mohawk, and nudging the head and neck geometry upward slightly to keep the proportions right while the mohawk spine still transitions smoothly from the head joint.

For the eyes, I'm enlarging the glow sphere and socket so they protrude more, and shifting the pupil slit forward to keep it readable against the bigger socket. Now I need to make sure my search strings match exactly before writing the edits, starting with the neck chain definition.

Writing neck chain code...

Fixing the duplicated tusk path definition...

Tapering the ring radius along the tusk and adding a single gold band near the base, then moving to redo the braid geometry with a new catmull spline path for the hair strands.

I'm adjusting the braid position lower on the chest since box-section geometry renders fuller than expected, keeping the bone rigged to the head. For the mohawk, I'm thickening it from [0.05, 0.016] to [0.085, 0.03] and bumping the bevel to 0.006 for a bolder look, leaving the feather accents at the braid ends as is.
